content.text: Tested using packaged fcrepo-4.0.0 instead of source-compiled
Same results. Application starts throwing errors at transaction #950.
Assuming this is related to the ObservationManager, maybe we should just use a System property instead.  This would let you override the automatic baseURL detection at runtime if you wanted to.

I have seen similar issues when doing large-scale ingest.  The first few 1000-object batches would load at roughly constant speed, but then ingest rate would slow down and eventually fcrepo4 would have an OutOfMemoryError related to garbage-collection.

Redeploying the fcrepo4 WAR file after each batch eliminates the problem.  So I've implemented using a System property instead of the ObservationManager to pass the baseURL, and I'm running an ingest test now to see if this resolves the issue.
I have run both of the scripts locally without hitting an OOM. The ingests progressively slow down, but the memory remains stable.
Scripts are attached: test.sh and test.sh.auth
, I would suggest ensuring that you can replicate the issue before committing to a fix.
If it is possible to replicate, it is also worth verifying that the issue is in both 4.0.0 and 4.0.1-SNAPSHOT.

I'll setup 4.0.0 and 4.0.1-SNAPSHOT on my VM to test the script.  But even if there is no OOM error, the slowdown is worrying.  I was able to ingest all 70K objects last October, but saw significant slowdown with larger batches.  Since then, all my attempts to ingest large numbers of objects have failed.

I was not able to reproduce any OOM or slowdowns with 4.0.1-SNAPSHOT.  I ran the stressTest shell script against a current master build and my baseurl-system-property, and got the same results.  I also did a few other tests that have sometimes created errors for me – creating 10K objects, updating a single object's title 10K times, etc. with the same results.
Meanwhile, my ingest process running aginst a baseurl-system-property build has gotten through 10K batches and is starting to slow down.

So I can't confirm this bug.  But there does appear to be some bug related to a long running time and/or a large number of operations, and my baseurl-system-property branch does not fix it.  In previous testing, I definitely found that I could load millions of files without triggering the problem.  But updating 10K objects reliably triggers the problem.  That process mostly involves PUT requests to creating nodes and update the RDF.
It looks like we will need to put the profiler on it to see where the increased time is happening. Will you have time for this? YourKit or the like?
I've setup YourKit and restarted my ingest process.  It should take around 8 hours to get to a significant slowdown and OutOfMemoryError.  When that happens, I'll create a YourKit profiling snapshot.

I've tried a couple of different strategies (starting YourKit before starting the ingest, waiting until the OOM occurs and then starting YourKit), but I haven't been able to get a profiling session to work either way.  If I run YourKit for the entire ingest process, it runs out of memory (even with 6GB of heap allocated).  If I try to start it once the error has occurred, then it hangs when trying to connect to the agent.

Do you have any advice for how to capture a very large session?  Would it be helpful to capture the first hour of the ingest process?  The error takes 6-8 hours to produce, but presumably the slowdown is already happening?
, In your comment from Jan 16th above [1], you stated that you were not able to recreate OOMs. Has that changed? Are you now able to reproduce Stefano's error?
If so, what script are you running?
As for YourKit, I wonder if taking an hour-long sample would be useful? If not, possibly taking two small samples separated by a couple of hours for comparison?
If you pass along your script, I can experiment on my side as well.

I was not able to produce errors or slowdowns with Stefano's scripts, or doing 10K runs of various GET/POST/PUT/PATCH operations.  But I am consistently hitting an OOM error related to garbage collection when I do real-world large-scale ingest, after around 10K objects are loaded (with 50K files and 20K authority records).  I was able to load all the files, so I am relatively sure that it's the metadata loading that's causing the problems.  This does HEAD requests to check whether objects exist, and then PUT requests with RDF/XML to load the metadata for objects that don't exist.  I haven't been able to simplify this process of creating this error, which now involves several GB of data files and our loading utility.
Tomorrow, I'll see if I can reproduce the error with a lighter-weight toolset.  Meanwhile, I'll take a couple of snapshots as the ingest runs and hopefully that'll be useful.
I've uploaded my first three snapshots here:

Whether because of the profiler or because my Dropbox sync was trying to sync, or both, the ingest progress has been dramatically slower than usual.  A batch typically takes about 30 minutes, but in this case, the first batch has not yet finished in more than 3 hours.
, I have been doing some profiling/experimenting, and discovered that for every new transaction, a new thread is added to the RepositoryChangeBus. Those threads do not go away.
I ran four scripted tests on the 4.0.0 release that simply creates batches of 500 UUIDPathMinter containers:
1. Authorization enable, with each create in its own transaction
3. No Authorization, with each create in its own transaction
Summary: OOM due to too many threads
Summary: consistent speed, no additional threads (44)
Summary: progressive slowing, each txn adds a permanent thread (1057)
Summary: consistent speed, no additional threads (38)
, For whatever reason, after downloading and gunzipping your snapshots, I get a "not a valid snapshot file" error when trying to load them.
I am able to load my own snapshots into YourKit locally.  I just downloaded and gunzipped the first snapshot and the md5 matches my original file (260b0261db43b68fe271108011e3cab0).
I'm using MacOSX, JDK 1.8.0_05 and YourKit 2014 (build 14116, 12/23/2014).  Maybe there is an incompatibility related to the platform/version?
So it sounds like you have a good way to reproduce this bug (too many transactions), but my problem is something else.  I have created a separate bug for the garbage collection issues:
, Based on re-running my tests documented in this ticket, the unbounded thread issue seems to have been resolved in master by this ticket:
Could you please verify on your end?
Ran fcrepo_stressTest.sh and ingested all 10,000 nodes witihin transactions without error.
Created stress test script (see attached file).
The script loops over the following tasks 10,000 times:
Fedora starts consistently throwing error around cycle #950.
After that, the app becomes unresponsive and Tomcat needs to be killed. See logfile excerpt.
Interestingly, on my ArchLinux development VM with less RAM and processor this does not happen.

renderedFields.description:
Created stress test script (see attached file).

The script loops over the following tasks 10,000 times:

  • open a transaction
  • create an object
  • commit the transaction

Fedora starts consistently throwing error around cycle #950.

After that, the app becomes unresponsive and Tomcat needs to be killed. See logfile excerpt.

Interestingly, on my ArchLinux development VM with less RAM and processor this does not happen.

Happy New Year!
